name: Position control
description: A position controller: the voltage it commands changes at Gain × (Setpoint angle − angle) − Rate gain × angular velocity. Connect it from a Rotational link (it reads the link's Angle and Angular velocity) to a Voltage source (it changes the source's Voltage), which in turn drives a Motor. Gain (V/(rad·s), default 5) sets how fast the voltage builds up for each radian the link is away from the setpoint; this is the integral action. Rate gain (V·s/rad, default 10) opposes the link's own angular velocity; this is the damping, the role a derivative term plays in a PID controller. Setpoint angle (rad, default 1, live) is where the link should end up, and can be moved during a run. The rate gain is not optional: the motor, link and voltage together make a loop with no damping of its own, which with integral action alone is unstable for any positive gain.
